newsitem.title: KUWAIT: First Sudan minister in Kuwait since 1990.
newsitem.headline: First Sudan minister in Kuwait since 1990.

text.p: A Sudanese minister arrived in Kuwait on Tuesday on the first visit by a Khartoum minister since Iraq's 1990 invasion of the Gulf Arab state.
The official Kuwait News Agency said minister of state at the foreign ministry Mustafa Osman Ismail "condemned" the invasion and said it was in "violation of international law".
Kuwait had downgraded ties and cut generous financial aid to several Arab states, including Sudan, which it accused of sympathising with Iraq during the 1990-91 Gulf crisis.
"Sudan certainly rejects the Iraqi occupation...and this is what we are stressing now," KUNA quoted the minister as saying.

Sudan was among three states which expressed reservations on an Arab League summit resolution in Cairo days after Iraq seized Kuwait. The resolution -- rejected by Iraq, Libya and the Palestine Liberation Organisation -- sanctioned the sending of Arab troops to Saudi Arabia.
The Arab troops later participated in the U.S.-led 1991 Gulf War against Iraq.
The Kuwait government and parliament had discussed in recent weeks in secret sessions the possibility of restoring ties with some Arab states which appeared to back Iraq during the crisis.
Diplomats say such moves might lack public support although there are some within the government who strongly back it.
